title: 生成式AI在高校图书馆特藏资源开发与创新创业教育融合中的应用研究
venue: 经济与管理发展研究
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: Against the backdrop of the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, university libraries are undergoing a value reconstruction from "knowledge warehouses" to "intelligent engines". This study focuses on the intersection of generative artificial intelligence, the development of special collections in university libraries, and innovation and entrepreneurship education, aiming to explore a new path for activating cultural heritage through technological innovation and empowering the cultivation of innovative talents with cultural resources. The paper first analyzes the intrinsic demands and contemporary opportunities of the development of special collection resources and innovation and entrepreneurship education. Furthermore, it systematically expounds the key technologies and application paradigms of generative AI in the links of text recognition, knowledge reconstruction, interactive presentation and creative derivation of special collection resources; On this basis, an integrated application model of "resource activation - scene construction - ability cultivation" was constructed and supported by cutting-edge practical cases at home and abroad. Finally, a dialectical analysis was conducted on the challenges of data, technology, ethics and talent faced during the integration process, and strategic prospects for the future were proposed. Research shows that generative AI is not only the core driving force for the "digital and intelligent" transformation of special collection resources, but also a key bridge to break down the barriers between cultural inheritance and innovative practice. It provides a practical and feasible solution for university libraries to reshape their educational functions and cultivate compound innovative and entrepreneurial talents in the AI era.

Autonomous Artificial Intelligence-Driven Smart Tree and Plant Medical System (منظومة الطب الذكي والذاتي للأشجار والنباتات عبر الذكاء الاصطناعي) TECHNICAL FIELD The present invention relates generally to agricultural technology, robotics, and artificial intelligence, and more particularly to an autonomous, multi-modal diagnostic and therapeutic system and classification framework for plant, tree, legume, vegetable, and fruit healthcare management. BACKGROUND AND SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION Traditional agricultural care lacks a structured medical taxonomy and real-time autonomous clinical intervention for individual plants and trees. The present invention solves this problem by providing a comprehensive, autonomous smart medical ecosystem that integrates multi-modal interfaces (voice, touch, writing, and gestures), smart cameras, self-learning AI databases, and specialized robotic applicators to diagnose, categorize, and treat plant pathologies across distinct botanical branches. BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS FIG. 1 (SYSTEM OVERVIEW): Illustrates the overall architecture of the smart medical system, showing the interaction between the Smart AI Core (10), Smart Cameras/Drones (20), Smart Diagnostic Devices (30), Smart Robotic Surgeons (40), and various botanical categories including Seedlings, Fruit Trees, and Legume/Vegetable Plants. FIG. 2 (DIAGNOSTIC METHODS): Depicts the user interface and AI diagnostic routines showing disease classifications such as Bark Canker (32), Leaf Fungus (34), and Internal Trunk Decay (36) processed via autonomous AI data points. FIG. 3 (TREATMENT MODALITIES): Shows the mechanical deployment mechanisms used by the robotic system, including Stem Injectors (44), Canopy Sprayers (48), and Basin Ointment Applicators (50) for liquid delivery, root-zone pouring, or topical cream application. FIG. 4 (TREE ANATOMY CLASSIFICATION): Demonstrates the specialized medical taxonomy of the invention, dividing plant care into internal tree medicine, trunk medicine, bark medicine, seedling medicine, legume medicine, fruit tree medicine, and vegetable medicine. FIG. 5 (OPERATIONAL DATA FLOW): Illustrates the data transmission loop between the AI Core, camera sensors, medical databases, smart devices, and human operator interfaces. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS System Architecture & Autonomous Core: The system comprises a centralized or distributed Smart AI Core (10) connected via a wireless network to high-definition Smart Cameras (20) and solar-powered charging/control stations. The AI core operates independently using self-learning algorithms to process real-time botanical health data. Multi-Modal User Interaction: Field operators and specialists interact with the system through Smart Diagnostic Devices (30) (such as handheld terminals or mobile tablets) supporting multi-modal inputs including voice commands, handwriting recognition, touch screens, and physical gestures. Specialized Botanical Medical Taxonomy (FIG. 4): The invention introduces a formal classification of plant medicine consisting of: Internal Tree Medicine (علم باطنية الأشجار الذكي): Diagnosing internal vascular and systemic health. Trunk Medicine (علم طب جذوع الأشجار الذكي): Structural and core support evaluation. Bark Medicine (علم طب لحاء الأشجار الذكي): Surface and protective layer healing. Sub-Category Specializations: Dedicated branches covering Seedlings (طب الشتول), Legumes (طب البقوليات), Fruits (طب الفواكه), and Vegetables (طب الخضروات), split further into large mature tree care and early-stage seedling care. Robotic Intervention & Treatment Modalities (FIG. 3): Treatment is executed either by human medical teams or Smart Robotic Surgeons (40) equipped with articulated robotic arms (46). The system delivers treatments via three primary clinical pathways: Basin Pouring / Soil Application (50): Liquid medications poured or dispensed directly into the tree basin. Stem / Trunk Injection (44): Direct micro-injection of therapeutic fluids into the woody core. Topical Ointment Application: Precise mechanical wiping or brushing of therapeutic medical balms onto localized diseased areas on the bark or leaves.

title: Цифровізація генеалогічних документів на основі технології автоматичного розпізнавання тексту

abstract: This study aimed to examine existing approaches and technologies for the digitisation of genealogical documents, drawing on international experience. This enabled more efficient organisation of digitisation processes and mechanisms for archive groups, their centralised storage, accelerated genealogical research, and improved user accessibility. The digitisation of archives had became a critically important aspect of preserving cultural heritage, particularly in the context of Russia's military aggression against Ukraine. The introduction of automatic text recognition technology had contributed to the optimisation of this process, facilitating access to information and enhancing the efficiency of research, particularly in the field of genealogy. The study analysed the operating principles of optical character recognition, its advantages, the features of ready-made solutions, and the functionality of software based on this technology. The strategy for digitisation in Ukraine was assessed, along with the challenges facing the archival sector in terms of digitisation and access to archive groups. The research also examined the outcomes of implementing automatic text recognition in leading archives worldwide, as well as the capabilities of online archives that offered contextual search functions. Particular attention was given to the opportunities afforded to researchers through the integration of such systems into archival operations, notably the ease of locating required information, the increased speed of data processing, and the provision of round-the-clock access to archival resources regardless of users’ geographical location. The study also reviewed the research of scholars involved in the development and implementation of optical character recognition in archival institutions. Drawing on international experience, the potential of modern Optical Character Recognition technologies to modernise the archival sector in Ukraine was identified, with positive implications for genealogical research and the preservation of cultural heritage. The practical value of the study lies in demonstrating the effectiveness of information technologies in improving the digitisation process of archival documents and enhancing access to them. The proposed recommendations aim to optimise the organisation of digital archives, improve document storage and retrieval processes, and accelerate genealogical research. These developments will contribute to the preservation of cultural heritage and improve access to archival information for users

title: scalable-htr: A Framework for Scalable and Reproducible Handwritten Text Recognition on Historical Documents
venue: ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: We present scalable-htr, a user-friendly open-source Python library for end-to-end segmentation and transcription of historical manuscripts. Built upon Kraken but extensible to other engines, the tool provides a framework for reproducible experimentation and efficient, large-scale inference on high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The tool facilitates systematic benchmarking across datasets and models by computing quantitative end-to-end metrics, and it generates interactive visualizations that allow users to qualitatively assess model adaptation to their target domains by inspecting segmentation and transcription results directly on the images. By combining systematic evaluation with scalable transcription, scalable-htr has been designed to assist researchers and cultural heritage professionals convert digitized manuscript collections into machine-readable data. The tool is demonstrated via a case study on medieval notarial manuscripts.

title: Znaczenie nowoczesnych metod cyfrowych dla badań nad misjami jezuickimi w Chinach
venue: Elementary Education in Theory and Practice (Jesuit University of Philosophy and Education Ignatianum)

abstract: This article addresses the application of modern digital tools in research on the Jesuit missionary heritage in China, using the project of a critical edition of Historia Sinarum Imperii (HSE) by Tomasz Szpot Dunin, SJ, as a case study. Drawing on the theoretical assumptions of digital humanities – understood not as a separate discipline but as a research strategy – the author analyzes the complete “digital workflow” employed in the project: from digitization and HTR (Handwritten Text Recognition) transcription, through text structuring and critical editing in the Classical Text Editor (CTE) environment, to advanced corpus analysis and the experimental use of large language models (LLMs) and RAG technology. The aim of the article is to demonstrate that the integration of technology into the research process does not replace the scholar but rather expands researchers’ cognitive capacities, enabling efficient interpretation of sources of considerable scale and complexity. In this context, the new possibilities available to researchers of archival texts using digital humanities methods are as significant as the careful selection of tools and technologies appropriate to the established research objectives.

title: WeSee: Enhancing Environmental Perception for Visually Challenged Individuals Through Multi-Modal AI Framework

abstract: In our country India, we have many brothers and sisters who cannot see properly and face big problems in their daily life [1]. Our project WeSee is like a good friend that helps them by using mobile camera to read text aloud and tell what objects are around them. Our special method uses two different text reading techniques together to get best results [2]. We also made object detection better for Indian conditions [3]. After testing with many images, we found that WeSee can read text with 95.1% correctness and find objects with 89% accuracy. This works very well on normal smartphones without needing expensive devices. KEYWORDS: Visual Assistance, Artificial Intelligence, Text Recognition, Object Detection, Ac-cessibility, Web Application.

title: VisionAid: An OpenCV-Based System Integrating Object Detection and OCR for Real-Time Scene Analysis
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: People with visual impairments often face difficulty in understanding their surroundings, especially in dynamic or unfamiliar environments. This study presents VisionAid, a realtime scene interpretation system that integrates object detection and optical character recognition (OCR) with a context-aware natural language generation pipeline to produce spoken descriptions of the environment. Built using OpenCV, YOLOv8, and EasyOCR, the system processes images captured from wearable and mobile cameras. Unlike many existing assistive systems that focus primarily on either object detection or text recognition, VisionAid performs OCR within detected object regions, enabling targeted text extraction from semantically relevant areas of the scene. The detected objects and extracted text are integrated and passed through a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) module, which generates coherent natural language scene descriptions delivered through text-to-speech. Performance was evaluated under controlled and real-world conditions using mobile cameras and a low-cost ESP32-CAM module. Results show that the system maintained reliable performance across varying lighting and backgrounds when higher-quality cameras were used, while accuracy declined under constrained hardware conditions. These findings highlight practical trade-offs between performance and hardware cost and demonstrate VisionAid's feasibility as a hands-free assistive vision system.

title: Vision Walk: AI-Driven Real-Time Visual Assistance System for Visually Impaired Navigation
venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: Visually impaired individuals face significant chal-lenges in perceiving their surroundings, detecting obstacles, read-ing text, and navigating safely. Traditional aids like white canes offer limited tactile feedback and lack contextual information. This paper presents Vision Walk, an AI-driven real-time visual assistance system that combines YOLOv8 for object detection, Tesseract OCR for text recognition, and spatial reasoning within a Flask-based web framework. The system operates entirely through a mobile browser, requiring no installation, and de-livers natural-language audio descriptions with directional cues (left, center, right). Experiments demonstrate that Vision Walk achieves object detection inference times of 40–80 ms, OCR processing of 70–140 ms, and end-to-end latency of 120–250 ms, making it suitable for real-time navigation. A user study with 12 visually impaired participants shows significant improvement in environmental awareness and navigation confidence. The system’s browser-based architecture ensures platform independence and cost-effectiveness, presenting a scalable solution for assistive technology.

title: Vision Beyond Sight : AI-Powered Assistance for the Visually Impaired
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), over 2.2 billion people worldwide experience some form of vision impairment, with nearly half of these cases remaining preventable or inadequately addressed. Despite recent advances in assistive technologies, existing solutions often suffer from limited language support, high dependency on internet connectivity, and insufficient contextual understanding of dynamic real-world environments. In this paper, we present VisionBeyondSight, a real-time, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven assistive framework designed to enhance environmental awareness for visually impaired individuals through multimodal visual interpretation and multilingual audio feedback. The proposed system integrates state-of-the-art computer vision and language models, including YOLOv11 (You Only Look Once, version 11) for real-time object and person detection, Pytesseract and Indic Optical Character Recognition (OCR) for multilingual text recognition, OpenCV for efficient video processing, and Google’s Gemini 2 Flash for context-aware scene understanding and natural language generation. A key contribution of this work is the seamless support for 22 Indian languages, addressing a critical accessibility gap in existing assistive applications such as Seeing AI and Be My Eyes. VisionBeyondSight operates through three adaptive modes—DESCRIBE, READ, and PEOPLE—enabling users to identify objects, read textual content, and perceive human presence using a single unified interface. Experimental evaluation demonstrates low-latency performance suitable for real-time deployment, reliable object detection and OCR accuracy across varied lighting and environmental conditions, and improved qualitative scene understanding through Large Language Model (LLM)-based reasoning. The system is lightweight, cost-effective, and deployable across multiple camera-enabled platforms, including mobile devices and desktops, highlighting its potential as a scalable and inclusive assistive solution.

title: Untethering EIT: An Integrated Wireless Tactile Interface for Human–Machine Interaction
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: Large-area tactile sensing is a core requirement for intelligent robots. However, traditional high-density sensor arrays face challenges due to complex wiring and high integration difficulty. These issues limit their industrial application. This article proposes a stable and flexible tactile sensing system based on electrical impedance tomography (EIT). At the hardware level, we developed a highly integrated and miniaturized data acquisition (DAQ) system. The developed DAQ system weighs 34 g, complementing a conformable flexible sensor with a thickness of 700$\mu$m. This design improves portability and achieves real-time dynamic mapping at 11.1 FPS. At the algorithmic level, we adopted a U-Net architecture to solve the nonlinear reconstruction challenges of EIT. Within a$58\times 58\,\,\text{mm}^{2}$sensing area, the model achieves a two-point spatial resolution limit of 7 mm and a mean multipoint localization error of 1.33 mm under multitouch scenarios. Furthermore, we utilized a CNN-BiLSTM model to decode complex spatiotemporal signals, achieving 96% accuracy for dynamic handwriting recognition and 85% in cross-user tests with ten participants, thereby demonstrating strong generalization capability. Finally, we deployed the system on an industrial robotic arm and a bionic hand. The system demonstrates high-fidelity contact sensing. It can also precisely identify small objects of 5 mm. The proposed EIT system provides a lightweight and scalable solution for industrial tactile perception and intelligent interaction.

title: Unstructured Data Parsing Method Based on Asymmetric Convolution and 3D Attention Residual Networks
venue: Electronics
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: Efficient parsing of manufacturing process data is a key enabler for the informatization of intelligent manufacturing systems. However, network isolation in aerospace-specific job shops makes large volumes of unstructured shop-floor data, such as handwritten production reports and equipment logs, inaccessible to existing information systems. To tackle this, we propose a comprehensive parsing framework that covers data acquisition, parsing, and structured output. For handwritten report parsing, we devise a collaborative pipeline comprising text detection via the Differentiable Binarization Network (DBNet); text recognition using an enhanced Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) that incorporates Asymmetric Convolution (AC) and a Simple Attention Module (SimAM)-based residual module (SimRes, short for SimAM ResNet), referred to as AC-SimRes-CRNN; and table structure extraction via TableMaster. The predicted table cell coordinates, detected text-region coordinates, and recognized text contents are subsequently aggregated to reconstruct complete tables, which are then exported as Excel files. Experiments on the CASIA-HWDB2x and IAM datasets show that AC-SimRes-CRNN achieves an Accurate Rate (AR) of 91.36% and a Correct Rate (CR) of 93.17% on Chinese handwritten text recognition and a Character Error Rate (CER) of 7.85% and a Word Error Rate (WER) of 26.83% on English handwritten text recognition, demonstrating competitive performance against representative methods. Ablation studies validate the contributions of both AC and SimRes. A case study on an aerospace equipment maintenance report further illustrates the component-level feasibility of the proposed workflow.

title: Truck License Plate Recognition Algorithm and Application Based on Large and Small Model Collaboration
venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)

abstract: To address issues such as heterogeneous camera perspectives, complex object detection tasks, and insufficient generalization capabilities of traditional algorithms in the governance of large trucks on highways, this paper proposes a multi-model intelligent monitoring algorithm based on the deep integration of the visual language model QWen-2.5-VL, the YOLO11 object detection model, and the PaddleOCRv5 text recognition model. The algorithm targets multi-angle images collected by road monitoring systems, including front, side, and rear views, to achieve four core functions: crane detection, license plate clarity assessment, license plate recognition, and axle visibility judgment. By constructing a multi-task independent parallel processing framework, it applies the semantic understanding capability of the visual language model and the precise positioning ability of the object detection algorithm to different task scenarios respectively.Experimental results on real-world scenario datasets show that the algorithm achieves an mAP of 94% in crane detection, an F1 score improvement to 96% in license plate clarity assessment, and an F1 score of 94.3% in axle visibility judgment. The research outcomes provide an efficient and reliable technical solution for the intelligent supervision of highway freight vehicles, with significant engineering application value.

title: TrOCR-Med: Revolutionizing Medical Data Handling with TransformerBased Handwritten Optical Character Recognition and Extraction
venue: Apple Academic Press eBooks
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: In the dynamic landscape of document digitalization, the task of text recognition persists as an enduring challenge. Traditional approaches have predominantly relied on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image comprehension and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for the generation of text at the character level. These methods are often supplemented with the inclusion of a post-processing language model to enhance overall accuracy. However, in this innovative research endeavor, we present a pioneering approach to text recognition, tailored explicitly to address the intricacies of recognizing handwritten text. Our methodology, aptly named TrOCR, represents a paradigm shift away from conventional practices. It does so by harnessing the transformative potential of pre-trained image Transformer and text Transformer models. TrOCR’s unique value proposition lies in its seamless integration of the Transformer architecture into the very essence of text recognition. This architectural choice empowers the model with the dual capability to comprehend images and generate text at a remarkable level of granularity, focusing on workpieces rather than individual 380characters. This strategic integration of Transformers is especially pertinent, given the Transformers’ remarkable success in NLP tasks, making them ideal candidates for this dual role in image and text understanding. The brilliance of the TrOCR model manifests in its elegant simplicity and unwavering effectiveness. Despite its streamlined approach, it exhibits exceptional accuracy and adaptability. TrOCR demonstrates the remarkable flexibility to undergo pre-training using extensive synthetic data, enabling it to develop a profound understanding of both visual and textual patterns. Subsequently, it can be fine-tuned with meticulous attention to detail, utilizing human-labeled datasets. This fine-tuning process aligns the model’s capabilities with real-world recognition tasks, enhancing its practical applicability. Perhaps the most compelling aspect of our research lies in the empirical validation of TrOCR’s capabilities. These tasks encompass the recognition of printed text, the deciphering of intricate handwritten text, and the tackling of challenges associated with scene text recognition. Our research represents a significant leap forward in the domain of text recognition. TrOCR’s innovative approach, blending image understanding and text generation within a unified Transformer architecture, promises higher precision and efficiency in the realm of document digitalization. By simplifying and unifying the recognition process while maintaining or even surpassing accuracy benchmarks, TrOCR emerges as a transformative technology with far-reaching implications for the field of document processing and digitization. title: Towards Implementing Compression and Decompression Techniques on FPGA for Deep Neural Networks
venue: IETE Journal of Research
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: Deep learning enables efficient analysis of complex data and finds applications across diverse domains such as healthcare, cybersecurity, and image and text recognition. However, implementing such applications in resource-constrained environments presents challenges due to limited memory, low processing power, and difficulty in handling computationally intensive tasks. This paper explores compression and decompression strategies to reduce memory overhead and enhance the computational efficiency of Deep Neural Network (DNN) inference. We propose a hardware-efficient clustering architecture that compresses the intermediate layer outputs of the DNN. Compressing the DNN layer outputs introduces sparsity by reducing the number of non-zero activations, which in turn lowers the computational complexity of subsequent layers. Further in this paper, we investigate the adaptability of Delta-Compressed Sparse Row (dCSR), a sparse matrix storage format originally developed for embedded systems, on FPGA and GPU platforms. We present a custom decompression unit for reconstructing sparse matrices represented in dCSR format. The proposed decompression architecture is implemented on an FPGA, and its performance is evaluated in terms of resource utilization, execution speed, and power consumption. We also implement a dCSR-based sparse DNN on a GPU that exhibits improvement in terms of sparse parameter storage and execution speed. The dCSR-based sparse DNNs achieve an average storage reduction of up to 4% and a maximum speedup of 1.92× compared to the baseline implementations on GPU.

title: TifinNet: CNN–Transformer Hybrid Architecture for Tifinagh Handwritten Recognition
venue: IEEE Access

abstract: Handwritten Optical Character Recognition (OCR) for the Tifinagh script remains a challenging task due to the script’s geometric complexity, high similarity among rotated characters, and the scarcity of annotated training data. Existing methods often struggle to handle the directional features and orientation variations characteristic of Tifinagh handwriting. To address these challenges, we propose TifinNet, a novel CNN–Transformer hybrid architecture tailored for handwritten Tifinagh character recognition. The model integrates geometry-aware convolutional layers with multi-scale attention mechanisms, enabling it to capture both fine-grained stroke details and broader contextual dependencies. Key contributions include the introduction of oriented convolution operations for modeling directional features across multiple angles, spatial attention modules to highlight character-relevant regions, and a hybrid training scheme that combines CTC and attention-based losses. Experimental results on the AMHCD dataset demonstrate that TifinNet achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. An ablation study further validates the importance of the oriented convolution layers and the hybrid loss design. At the sequence level, the model delivers higher word recognition accuracy and lower edit distances compared to existing approaches, highlighting its practical effectiveness for end-to-end text recognition. Overall, TifinNet provides a robust and efficient solution for Tifinagh OCR and offers broader insights into the design of CNN–Transformer architectures for low-resource script recognition.

title: The Use of the Write It Arabic Application in Developing the Writing Skill of Beginner Arabic Leaners: A Descriptive Study

abstract: Effective mastery of Arabic script remains a fundamental challenge for non-native beginners, necessitating the evaluation of digital learning tools. This study aims to describe the Write It Arabic application and explain how it is used to develop writing skills for beginner learners of the Arabic language. The researcher employed a descriptive method by collecting information related to the application’s features, its method of presenting Arabic letters, and the training mechanisms provided to users. The findings indicate that the application offers an appropriate learning environment for beginners, as it presents the form and pronunciation of each letter, followed by a visual demonstration of the steps for writing it, before guiding learners to a practical training stage that relies on direct recognition of handwriting. The results also show that the program provides several useful features, including short lessons, immediate feedback, and the ability to repeat exercises, in addition to assessment tools that help evaluate learners’ proficiency levels. However, the study also identifies several limitations, such as the application’s focus on letters only without progressing to word-level writing, the presence of advertisements in certain versions, and the limited availability of free content. The novelty of this study lies in its specific focus on the mechanical-kinesthetic features of handwriting recognition in Arabic MALL (Mobile Assisted Language Learning). The study concludes that the Write It Arabic application can serve as an effective tool to support the teaching and learning of basic writing skills, both in classroom settings and self-directed learning contexts, provided that further development is undertaken to include higher levels of writing skills.

abstract: This paper explores the role and importance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in modern libraries. With the rapid growth of digital information and changing user expectations, traditional library practices are no longer enough. AI tools like machine learning, chatbots, natural language processing, and data analytics are helping libraries manage their operations more efficiently. AI supports library tasks such as cataloguing, classification, circulation, and collection development. It can automatically organize resources, generate metadata, and detect duplicates, which reduces errors and saves time. This allows librarians to focus more on assisting users and supporting research. User services have also improved through AI. Chatbots and virtual assistants offer 24/7 help, while recommendation systems suggest books or articles based on users’ interests. In digital libraries, AI assists in digitization, text recognition, summarization, translation, and preserving digital content. In research libraries, AI supports literature review, citation analysis, plagiarism detection, and trend identification. It helps scholars find relevant information quickly and explore connections between different fields. However, using AI also comes with challenges. Ethical concerns, data privacy, bias in algorithms, and the need for technical skills must be considered. AI should assist librarians rather than replace them. Proper planning, training, and responsible use are essential for success. In short, AI has the potential to transform libraries into smarter, user-focused, and more efficient spaces. When applied thoughtfully, it can improve services, support research, and ensure that libraries remain relevant in today’s digital world.

abstract: Extracting subtitles from video frames plays a crucial role in automated captioning systems. This study presents a three-stage framework consisting of data preparation, subtitle detection, and subtitle recognition. title: TamOCR: A Lightweight LLM-Assisted OCR Framework for Digitizing Tamil-Brahmi Inscriptions

abstract: The digitisation of Tamil–Brahmi inscriptions is essential for safeguarding South India’s earliest written heritage, yet real-world OCR deployment is still challenged by weathered stone surfaces, broken or missing glyphs, inconsistent lighting, and highly variable carving styles. In response to survey findings that highlighted the need for modular and resilient OCR pipelines, this work introduces TamOCR, a lightweight, LLM-assisted OCR framework tailored for Tamil–Brahmi inscription digitisation. The framework combines a robust pre-processing stage for contrast enhancement and noise reduction, a segmentation module that isolates glyphs from complex stone backgrounds, and a recognition stage driven by compact vision models tuned for low-resource execution environments. To mitigate recognition ambiguities, TamOCR employs a lightweight language-model–based reconstruction layer that performs context-aware correction, symbol disambiguation, and transliteration refinement. We evaluate the framework on diverse inscription datasets with varying degradation levels and show substantial gains in character-level accuracy, word-level recognition stability, and robustness when compared with conventional OCR engines and heavier neural architectures. Owing to its modular design, the framework can be deployed on resource-constrained platforms, making it suitable for field archaeology, museum applications, and large-scale digital archiving. This work offers an early practical realisation of Tamil–Brahmi OCR using a lightweight LLM and provides a feasible pathway toward scaling the preservation of ancient scripts.

title: TLive-Omni: An Omni-Modal Understanding Model for E-Commerce Live Streaming
venue: arXiv (Cornell University)

abstract: E-commerce live streaming requires omni-modal understanding of noisy, temporally extended streams, where product facts are distributed across speech, video frames, product images, overlaid text, and user queries. We present TLive-Omni, an omni-modal understanding model tailored to live-commerce scenarios. It maps image, video, audio, and text inputs into a unified representation space. For long-form live streaming analysis, we introduce Per-vGrid, a timestamped token organization that groups each video grid with its temporally corresponding audio within explicit boundary tokens to facilitate temporal alignment. We design a three-stage supervised training recipe that progressively develops live-commerce understanding, from omni-modal perception to instruction-following responses. We then propose Faithful-RFT, a reinforcement fine-tuning stage that further improves answer faithfulness and expression quality while meeting real-time demands, scoring final responses directly with task-verifiable feedback rather than optimizing for reasoning-style exploration during rollout. Moreover, TLive-Omni is supported by a scenario-oriented atomic capability taxonomy and a compact data production engine that converts live-commerce audio, image, and video streams into training signals for speech recognition, speaker analysis, product visual grounding, text recognition, temporal grounding, video dense caption, and omni-modal QA, etc. For scalable training, a synchronized length-grouped sampler reduces padding while preserving comparable workloads across workers, while a lightweight dynamic sampling strategy regenerates rollout groups with near-zero reward variance to maintain meaningful relative advantages for GRPO. Experiments on e-commerce live streaming benchmarks demonstrate strong performance across live-commerce domain tasks, together with excellent generalization on general benchmarks.

abstract: Evaluating handwritten answer scripts by hand has long been a resource-intensive process, prone to inconsistency and examiner fatigue. Recent developments in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning (ML), Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and Natural Language Processing (NLP) offer a technically credible path toward automating this workflow. This paper presents an ML-driven system designed to evaluate handwritten answer sheets without manual intervention. The pipeline begins with OCR-based conversion of scanned scripts into machine-readable text, followed by NLP preprocessing and multi-strategy scoring. Evaluation draws on keyword matching, semantic similarity, and syntactic analysis, with transformer-based models—BERT and Sentence-BERT—paired with cosine similarity and Jaccard index metrics to achieve greater precision. The resulting system produces consistent, bias-free scores, generates detailed performance reports for individual students, and can operate at scale across diverse exam formats, file types, and languages. By uniting document recognition with semantic understanding, the proposed solution addresses key shortcomings in fairness, turnaround time, and transparency that persist in conventional grading practice. title: Structure-Aware Multi-Task Learning for Robust Vision-Language OCR

abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) remains a core component of document understanding systems, yet existing OCR pipelines often struggle with complex layouts and incorrect reading order in real-world documents. Recent vision-language (VL) models have improved text recognition by jointly modeling visual and textual information, but document structure is still commonly treated as an implicit or downstream problem. As a result, layout misinterpretation has become a major source of errors in end-to-end document parsing. In this work, we propose a structure-aware multi-task learning framework built upon a compact vision-language OCR model. The proposed approach jointly optimizes text recognition, layout semantic classification, and reading order prediction within a unified training pipeline. By introducing explicit structural supervision as tightly coupled auxiliary objectives, the model is encouraged to internalize document-level organization while preserving the efficiency and modularity of practical OCR systems. Extensive experiments on diverse document benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves layout understanding and reading order accuracy, while also yielding gains in overall document parsing robustness. In particular, the structure-aware training framework shows clear advantages on documents with complex layouts and multilingual content, without introducing significant inference overhead. These results suggest that explicit modeling of document structure is a crucial step toward robust and scalable OCR-based document understanding.

title: SqueezeNet-driven AI framework for OCR of handwritten English characters and digits

abstract: Optical character recognition (OCR) plays a pivotal role in automated data entry, document digitization, and intelligent user interfaces, particularly as digital content continues to expand across diverse applications. This study investigates the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) strategies for classifying handwritten English characters and digits, employing the orange3 platform and a dataset of 2,728 images sourced from Kaggle, partitioned into 70% training and 30% testing sets. A SqueezeNet-based feature extraction approach was implemented to generate 1,000 discriminative features, which were subsequently used to train multiple ML classifiers, including support vector machine (SVM), decision tree (DT), and random forest (RF). Experimental evaluation revealed that the RF classifier achieved the highest accuracy of 99.3%, outperforming DT (90.3%) and SVM (89.9%). These findings highlight the effectiveness of lightweight deep learning architectures such as SqueezeNet in enhancing OCR performance, while demonstrating the robustness of ensemble learning methods in achieving near-perfect classification accuracy. The proposed framework underscores the potential of combining efficient feature extraction with ML classifiers to advance OCR systems for handwritten text recognition in real-world applications.

title: SpiS-GAN: Spiral-Modulated Handwriting Synthesis with Star Operation
venue: arXiv (Cornell University)

abstract: Training robust handwriting recognition (HTR) systems requires massive amounts of annotated data, which is often difficult to acquire. While synthetic handwriting generation offers a practical solution to expand training sets, existing models struggle with several core issues. First, previous approaches, even MLP-based models fail to effectively trace cursive handwriting due to fixed-grid spatial receptive field. Second, their CNN-relied discriminators usually lose structural details through aggressive downsampling, making broken connections difficult to detect. Third, existing architectures are either limited to linear feature interactions or too expensive for high-resolution synthesis. Finally, existing approaches lack explicit edge constraints, often resulting in blurred stroke boundaries. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Spiral-Modulated Handwriting Synthesis framework based on Generative Adversarial Networks (SpiS-GAN). Our generator employs Star-Spiral Blocks combining proposed Modulated Elliptical SpiralFC with the star operation to capture spatial relationships and efficiently follow complex handwriting stroke trajectories, while a Spiral-Modulated discriminator is introduced for multi-domain flaws detection. Additionally, we introduce a Sobel-Regularized Edge Reconstruction Loss that provides edge guidance, ensuring every character remains clear and legible. Evaluations on the English and Vietnamese datasets demonstrate that SpiS-GAN significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art models. The generated images are highly authentic, accurately preserve the original writer's style across languages, and successfully lower error rates when training downstream HTR systems.

abstract: We proposes SeqAttend-OCR, an attention-guided bidirectional sequence modeling architecture for lightweight text recognition. Evaluated against five representative models on benchmarks spanning natural scenes, synthetic text, and multilingual documents, SeqAttend-OCR achieves $97.8 \%$ recognition accuracy with only 42 million parameters, outperforming comparably sized baselines by $2.3-4.1\%$ on low-quality images. title: SVTRv2X: Enhanced scene text recognition via self-distilled mixture-of-experts
venue: PLoS ONE

abstract: Scene Text Recognition (STR) is a fundamental component of intelligent perception systems and plays a crucial role in a wide range of real-world applications such as autonomous driving, document understanding, and human–computer interaction. STR still faces several challenges in practical applications, including high sensitivity to spatial perturbations, limited representational capacity of lightweight Connectionist Temporal Classification(CTC)-based models, and the difficulty of handling diverse text styles within a single unified architecture. Although SVTRv2 enhances the recognition ability of CTC models through a combination of local and global mixing mechanisms, its robustness and generalization capability remain insufficient when dealing with geometric distortions, complex backgrounds, or text with large stylistic variations. To address these issues, we propose SVTRv2X, an enhanced STR framework built upon SVTRv2 that integrates three complementary improvement modules. The Jumble Module strategically rearranges input patches before the patch embedding stage, fundamentally reducing the model’s reliance on fixed spatial structures and significantly improving robustness to rotated, misaligned, and irregular text. The Self-Distillation Module transfers deep-layer knowledge to shallow features, effectively strengthening early-stage representations while maintaining lightweight inference. The Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Module expands model capacity through sparsely activated expert networks, allowing specialized processing of different text styles without introducing substantial computational overhead. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SVTRv2X achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple STR benchmarks, substantially advancing the model’s recognition capability in real-world scene text scenarios.

abstract: Handwritten text recognition is important for digitising historical records, educational documents, government files, and other handwritten materials. To solve these problems, the paper describes an AI-based handwritten text recognition system for Indian scripts using deep learning. The system combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), and Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) to recognise handwritten text lacking needing to separate each character. The CNN extracts important visual features from document images, while the BiLSTM captures the context of character sequences. The CTC decoding layer pairs the features with the correct text, permitting efficient end-to-end prediction. The model is tested on handwritten Telugu and Hindi datasets and evaluated utilizing metrics including Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, Character Error Rate (CER), and Word Error Rate (WER). abstract: Multilingual document and scene text understanding plays an important role in applications such as search, finance, and public services. To make such multilingual, multi-task annotation feasible, we design a hybrid pipeline for Document Parsing and TEC-VQA. It combines automated filtering and scoring with MLLM-assisted labeling and lightweight native-speaker verification, greatly reducing manual labeling while maintaining high quality. We evaluate several leading multimodal models and observe pronounced performance degradation on low-resource Southeast Asian languages, highlighting substantial remaining gaps in multilingual document and scene text understanding. We believe SEA-Vision will help drive global progress in document and scene text understanding.

title: Reliable Kazakh Handwritten Text Recognition with Error-Correcting Output Codes and Redundant Ensembles

abstract: Handwritten text recognition systems that serve real users must be more than accurate—they must remain reliable under noise, device constraints, and occasional compute faults. We study reliability-centered Kazakh handwritten text recognition by combining error-correcting output codes with redundant lightweight ensembles and a simple watchdog for selective prediction. Each character is mapped to a structured codeword and the network predicts code bits; inference uses nearest-neighbor Hamming decoding with optional parity checks, converting small logit perturbations into correctable events. We evaluate robustness under controlled corruptions (blur, noise, occlusion), quantization, and bit-flip fault injection. In bit-flip simulations, error-correcting-code decoding reduces misclassification from 78.73% to 2.27% at p = 0.10, and from 90.69% to 23.43% at p = 0.20, while correctly recovering 86.66% of faulted trials at p = 0.10. With three diverse replicas, bit-wise ensemble fusion further lowers error to 0.01% at p = 0.10, outperforming label voting. Finally, the watchdog reduces failure-without-warning to 0.01% at 64.95% coverage, enabling practical coverage–risk trade-offs. Together, these results show that classical redundancy and coding concepts translate naturally to modern deep handwritten text recognition, providing a practical path to robust and deployable recognition for Kazakh and other under-resourced scripts.

abstract: The task of rod calculus formula recognition aims to automatically convert the arrangement of counting rods in ancient mathematical texts into corresponding editable computer encodings. This process requires that the generated encoding not only accurately represents the mathematical semantics but also maintains high morphological consistency with the original symbols. Existing optical character recognition (OCR) methods face severe challenges in handling such formulas. Ancient document images commonly suffer from degradations such as geometric distortion, ink bleeding, wormholing, paper wrinkling, which lead to broken or adherent strokes of the rod numerals; character scales vary significantly, with the area of the character “元” being up to three times that of “0”, and column-width constraints often cause symbols to be squeezed or overlapped; the class distribution is extremely imbalanced, with the vertical form of “1” accounting for 15% while “太” only 0.18%, exacerbating training difficulty. To address these issues, this paper proposes a CRNN-FPT recognition framework that integrates a feature pyramid network with Transformer. This framework fuses ResNet and feature pyramid network to extract multi-scale features, designs a partial depthwise convolution module to enhance anti-degradation capability, and employs a Transformer encoder for sequence modeling to capture long-range spatial dependencies. Meanwhile, a hybrid loss function is used for joint supervision, which focuses on hard-to-recognize samples, improves intra-class feature compactness, and enhances the model’s ability to distinguish confusable symbols. Experimental results demonstrate that the CRNN-FPT method significantly outperforms existing text recognition models on rod calculus formula recognition, achieving a 1.5 percentage-point improvement in text-line recognition accuracy and a 1.48 percentage-point increase in character recognition rate.

title: Recent Trends in Data-Efficient Scene Text Recognition: A Survey on Zero-Shot and Few-Shot Learning
venue: ITM Web of Conferences
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: Scene Text Recognition (STR) is widely applied in computer vision for extracting and interpreting textual information from natural scene images and in this survey, a comprehensive analysis of Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL) and Few-Shot Learning (FSL) approaches for STR is presented. The limitations of traditional Optical Character Recognition (OCR) systems, which rely heavily on large annotated datasets, are addressed through data-efficient learning paradigms. It is demonstrated that ZSL is utilized to recognize unseen text categories without requiring prior labelled examples, while FSL is employed to enable learning from a limited number of annotated samples. Various methodologies are examined, including semantic embedding techniques, transfer learning strategies, meta-learning frameworks, and generative models such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), through which robust feature representations are learned. In ZSL, relationships between seen and unseen classes are established using semantic representations, whereas in FSL, rapid adaptation is achieved through optimization-based and metric-based approaches such as Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML), Prototypical Networks, and Siamese Networks. Transformer-based architectures and vision-language models are also incorporated to enhance performance under limited data conditions. In this paper a comparative analysis between ZSL and FSL is conducted based on training data requirements, generalization ability, feature extraction mechanisms, and application domains. Also discuss benchmark datasets such as SynthText, ICDAR, SVT, and Synth90k are utilized for evaluation, and performance is measured using metrics including Word Recognition Accuracy, Character Recognition Accuracy, Edit Distance, Unseen Class Accuracy, and Harmonic Mean. Key challenges are identified, including semantic-visual domain gaps, high intra-class variability, domain shifts, data scarcity, and overfitting, while additional issues such as noisy backgrounds, distorted text, and low-resolution images are also considered. It is concluded that ZSL and FSL are capable of improving scalability, adaptability, and efficiency in STR systems by reducing dependency on large labelled datasets, and future research directions are suggested in areas such as self-supervised learning, domain adaptation, multimodal embeddings, and the development of specialized evaluation benchmarks.

title: Real-Time Vehicle License Plate Recognition Using YOLOv9 and OCR Framework
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: Vehicle License Plate Recognition (VLPR) is a fundamental component of intelligent transportation systems, enabling automated vehicle identification for traffic monitoring, law enforcement, and smart city applications. In densely populated urban environments, license plate recognition remains challenging due to occlusion, motion blur, varying illumination, diverse plate layouts, and multilingual character usage. In the context of Bangladesh, vehicle license plates commonly contain both Bangla and English characters, further increasing recognition complexity. This paper presents a realtime vehicle license plate detection and recognition framework based on a deep learning driven object detection model integrated with an optical character recognition (OCR) pipeline. A YOLOv9-based detector is employed to accurately localize license plates from video streams, followed by region-of-interest extraction and multilingual text recognition with postprocessing validation. The proposed system is evaluated on a custom dataset captured under diverse urban traffic conditions, including dense traffic flow, variable lighting, and partial occlusion. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a detection Precision-Recall (F1-score) 0.99 while the OCR module attains an overall character recognition accuracy above 99.97%, maintaining real-time performance at more than 35 frames per second. These results indicate that the proposed framework is robust, efficient, and suitable for practical deployment in real-world traffic surveillance and intelligent transportation systems.

title: Real-Time Guidance and Personalised Support System for Visually Impaired Individuals
venue: International Conference on Expert Clouds and Applications (ICOECA)
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: Individuals with visual impairments face significant challenges when performing daily activities on their own due to limited access to visual information. Recent advancements in mobile computing, computer vision, and speech technologies have made it possible to create intelligent assistive applications. This paper introduces a real-time guidance and personalised support system designed for visually impaired users using a mobile-based approach. The proposed system is developed using Flutter and includes various assistive features, such as object and person detection, text recognition, barcode scanning, color identification, currency and medicine recognition, and emergency assistance. These vision-based features use Google ML Kit’s pretrained convolutional neural network (CNN) models, allowing for efficient on-device processing without needing custom model training. The system works through a voice-driven interaction mechanism, where user commands are analyzed to activate the right assistive module. The detected information is turned into audio feedback using text-to-speech technology, which helps users understand their surroundings better. Experimental results show that the system improves situational awareness, safety, and independence for visually impaired users while maintaining real-time performance on standard smartphones.

title: Real-Time Allergen Detection in Packaged Foods Using OCR and NLP on Mobile Platform
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: Food allergies represent a significant public health concern, particularly when consumers are unable to accurately identify allergens in packaged foods due to challenges such as complex ingredient terminology and the presence of scientific names. Manual interpretation of ingredient labels often results in confusion and increases the risk of accidental allergen exposure. This study aims to develop a mobile application to address this issue through real-time allergen detection using Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and Natural Language Processing (NLP). The system allows users to scan food labels using a smartphone camera, extract textual content via OCR, and detect potential allergens by comparing tokenized outputs against a curated allergen name database. The application was developed using the adapted Waterfall Model and implemented as a fully functional Flutter-based mobile app. Backend services were hosted using Google Cloud Run, while a Gemini AI chatbot was integrated to deliver personalized food allergy guidance. Performance evaluation conducted on 40 food label images using text recognition metrics, Character Error Rate (CER) and Word Error Rate (WER) have yielded average scores of 4.76 % and 13.72 %, respectively, demonstrating the reliability of the OCR in allergen identification. The study expects to benefit a broad spectrum of users including individuals with food allergies, caregivers, educational institutions and health organizations. By improving food safety and awareness, the system contributes to the achievement of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3: Good Health and Well-being. Future work will focus on enhancing image preprocessing, expanding the allergen database, and enabling offline functionality to further improve system robustness.

title: Raspberry Pi based Assistive Reading System for Visually Impaired People
venue: International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: Assistive technologies have played a crucial role in enhancing accessibility among the visually impaired by offering them independence in reading printed text. In this paper, the design and development of an Assistive Reading System based on Raspberry Pi that combines image capture, Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and Text-to-Speech (TTS) technologies is presented. The system uses Pi Camera to take pictures of textual information that is then handled using OCR techniques that are implemented in Python to obtain readable text. The text that is extracted is then translated into a speech output, which provides users to listen to the information via the speaker. In addition, the system will use a Liquid Crystal Display (LCD) to show the IP address of the device, which will enable people to view the captured images remotely via a web interface. This will allow caregivers or users to view and ensure that the content captured is accurate in real time. The system proposed is small, affordable, and easy to use, thus, feasible to implement. Evaluation under experimental conditions indicates consistent text recognition and speech generation under different environmental conditions. The system will improve considerably in terms of accessibility and independence among users with visual impairment and offers an efficient substitute to the existing assistive reading solutions.

abstract: Pre-Alpha Ethiopic (Geʽez / Amharic) recognition model — PP-OCRv6 medium fine-tune Status: preliminary / pre-Alpha. This deposit is an early public checkpoint, not a finished production model. Better versions are planned as soon as additional medieval and pre-modern Ethiopic ground truth can be annotated and curated. High-quality line-level GT for this domain is scarce and almost nonexistent in open corpora; the base PP-OCRv6 medium model itself only saw Geʽez as synthetic data. Treat current scores as provisional and expect material gains once real manuscript coverage grows. Line-level handwritten (and mixed handwritten/print-adjacent) text recognition model for Ethiopic-script materials, trained mainly on Geʽez with some Amharic, covering roughly 49 medieval / pre-modern manuscripts drawn from collections such as the British Library, Princeton University Library, vHMML / EMML, BnF, Vatican, Walters, and others. Fine-tuned in eScriptorium (default recognition training) with kraken from the public PP-OCRv6 (medium) weights (~15.9M parameters). The fine-tuned artifact metadata records variant: medium, PPOCRv6Model, baseline segmentation, and _kraken_min_version: 7.1.0. Architecture PP-OCRv6 CTC line recognizer as implemented in kraken ≥ 7.1 (feature/ppocrv6_rec): lightweight convolutional backbone + non-recurrent sequence neck. This record is the medium size class (not tiny/small). See the base model card for architecture details. Uses Intended: exploratory HTR on medieval / pre-modern Ethiopic-script manuscripts (primarily Geʽez; some Amharic), especially material similar to the training manuscripts listed below. Not intended (yet): a general-purpose Ethiopic OCR/HTR solution for all periods, print traditions, or hands; production pipelines that need stable orthography or abbreviation handling without human review. Roadmap: successive Zenodo versions under the same concept DOI as annotation volume and diversity increase. Transcription guidelines, Normalization, and Transformations Training and the reported ketos test metrics used Unicode NFD and whitespace normalization (ketos test -u NFD -n), consistent with the base PP-OCRv6 medium recipe. No claim is made that all contributing manuscripts share a single diplomatic/normalized transcription guideline; residual inconsistency (punctuation, word division, Geʽez punctuation marks such as ፡ ። ፤, and related letter confusions) is visible in the confusion list from evaluation. Bias, Risks, and Limitations Data scarcity: Open, reusable medieval Ethiopic HTR ground truth is extremely limited. This pre-Alpha model is trained on a comparatively small private PAGE-XML collection (~367 pages / ~18k text lines in the dump used for evaluation). Coverage is biased toward the hands, layouts, imaging, and transcription habits of those sources. Optimistic metrics: The hold-out CER/WER below is a random page split of the same dump, not a manuscript-disjoint or out-of-collection test. Generalization to unseen libraries, centuries, or scripts-within-Ethiopic may be substantially worse. Base-model gap: Upstream PP-OCRv6 medium listed Geʽez as synthetic-only; this fine-tune is an attempt to close that gap with real pages, but remains early. Language mix: Geʽez-dominant with some Amharic; do not assume balanced bilingual performance. Prefer human verification for scholarly editions; expect future versions to obsolete this checkpoint. title: PoM: A Linear-Time Replacement for Attention with the Polynomial Mixer
venue: arXiv (Cornell University)
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: This paper introduces the Polynomial Mixer (PoM), a novel token mixing mechanism with linear complexity that serves as a drop-in replacement for self-attention. PoM aggregates input tokens into a compact representation through a learned polynomial function, from which each token retrieves contextual information. We prove that PoM satisfies the contextual mapping property, ensuring that transformers equipped with PoM remain universal sequence-to-sequence approximators. We replace standard self-attention with PoM across five diverse domains: text generation, handwritten text recognition, image generation, 3D modeling, and Earth observation. PoM matches the performance of attention-based models while drastically reducing computational cost when working with long sequences. The code is available at https://github.com/davidpicard/pom.

title: Peer Review Report For: Enhancing Transformer-Based Language Models for Hungarian Handwritten Text Recognition [version 1; peer review: 1 approved with reservations]

abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is still working on making a multilingual model that incorporates the Hungarian language. We introduce a hybrid Hungarian and English model, one of the biggest challenges is to recognize handwritten text. We are going to investigate a set of models in this research, such as TrOCR large-handwritten, leveraging PULI-BERT, and Roberta-base with Diet models. The digitization of documents, and the preservation of cultural heritage specifically, has long been a research problem related to text recognition. We use an extensive text on the recognition approach using pre-trained visual and language transformer models. We pre-train the TrOCR proposed by Microsoft researchers for both large and base models at the first phase and then fine-tune them on human data at the second stage. Then, leverage new pre-trained transformers models such as Roberta-base, and PULI-BERT, as decoders and Diet, Vit, and Beit as encoder models at the pre-training phase on generated synthetic data and then fine-tune them on a small amount of human-annotated data provided by (DH-Lab) researchers with augmentation and without augmentation. Developed using tiny-scale Synthetic data of around three-million-line text open-source corpus, and subsequently refined using tiny person-labeled datasets. Experiments showed that the best CER is 3.681 in the TrOCR large handwritten, and the best WER is 16.091 by leveraging the PULI-BERT with the Deit model. These fine-tuned models outperform the currently existing state-of-the-art TrOCR models on historical Hungarian handwriting, according to the benchmark results on the János Arany dataset.

abstract: PP-OCRv6 (tiny) multilingual text recognition base model Description This is the tiny variant (~0.69M parameters) of a family of PP-OCRv6 text-line recognition models (tiny, small, medium) for kraken. The models are trained from scratch with baseline + bounding polygon data with a very diverse corpus containing historical, contemporary and born-digital document line images, handwritten and machine-printed, covering 44 languages across 10 scripts (Arabic, Armenian, Cyrillic, Ethiopic, Georgian, Greek, Hebrew, Latin, Malayalam, and Syriac). Architecture PP-OCRv6 is a conventional CTC-based line recognizer consisting of a lightweight convolutional backbone and a non-recurrent sequence-modelling neck. The original architecture published as part of PaddlePaddle has been adapted for historical ATR by: increasing line height to 128px uncapping line width/CTC label budget replacing the optimizer with Adam+Muon Uses This is a base model that is supposed to produce usable output across a wide range of scripts and materials out of the box while also allowing fine-tuning with ease. It should offer similar accuracy and generalization to VLM-based recognizers without hallucinations and with vastly higher throughput. This medium variant model achieves the highest scores on the test set, tiny and small trade accuracy for inference speed and a smaller memory footprint. Transcription guidelines, Normalization, and Transformations No attempt has been made to normalize the source datasets to a single set of transcription guidelines; the corpus mixes conventions, so inconsistent output is to be expected, in particular for Latin-script European manuscripts which mix large datasets such as CATMuS and TRIDIS that have very different approaches to transcription. Text was normalized to Unicode NFD and whitespace was normalized during training and evaluation. Bias, Risks, and Limitations The training corpus is heavily skewed towards a handful of high-resource languages (English, French, German, Latin, Dutch, Middle French, ...). Languages with little real training material show markedly higher error rates and will require fine-tuning for practical use. Because transcription conventions are inconsistent across sources, the model may resolve abbreviations or expand glyphs unpredictably. The synthetic data used for training was created with the pangoline tool which is limited to approximating modern, machine-printed text. For the languages/scripts present only as synthetic data (Classical Armenian, Geʽez) and to a lesser extent those sharing the Latin script (Irish, Latvian, Lithuanian, Romanian, Serbian, Slovenian), real-world accuracy is probably limited. title: PP-OCRv5: A Specialized 5M-Parameter Model Rivaling Billion-Parameter Vision-Language Models on OCR Tasks
venue: arXiv (Cornell University)
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: The advent of "OCR 2.0" and large-scale vision-language models (VLMs) has set new benchmarks in text recognition. However, these unified architectures often come with significant computational demands, challenges in precise text localization within complex layouts, and a propensity for textual hallucinations. Revisiting the prevailing notion that model scale is the sole path to high accuracy, this paper introduces PP-OCRv5, a meticulously optimized, lightweight OCR system with merely 5 million parameters. We demonstrate that PP-OCRv5 achieves performance competitive with many billion-parameter VLMs on standard OCR benchmarks, while offering superior localization precision and reduced hallucinations. The cornerstone of our success lies not in architectural expansion but in a data-centric investigation. We systematically dissect the role of training data by quantifying three critical dimensions: data difficulty, data accuracy, and data diversity. Our extensive experiments reveal that with a sufficient volume of high-quality, accurately labeled, and diverse data, the performance ceiling for traditional, efficient two-stage OCR pipelines is far higher than commonly assumed. This work provides compelling evidence for the viability of lightweight, specialized models in the large-model era and offers practical insights into data curation for OCR. The source code and models are publicly available at https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR.

title: PHDReader: police handwritten document recognition method based on VLM with EI-LFT using FP-EESR and MFE-GLS
venue: Scientific Reports
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: Police handwritten document recognition plays an increasingly important role in improving new quality combat capability of public security organs. To address the challenges associated with the recognition, this paper proposes a police handwritten document recognition method based on Qwen3VL with EI-LFT using FP-EESR and MFE-GLS. Firstly, Fusion Preprocessing with Edge Enhancement for Super-Resolution Reconstruction(FP-EESR) was used to enhance the handwriting features of handwritten Chinese characters while Multi-scale Feature Extraction using Global-Local-Semantic (MFE-GLS) was employed to extract "global-local-semantic" fusion features to improve recognition performance, as well as Embedding Instruction & LoRA Fine-Tuning (EI-LFT) was utilized to fine tune Qwen3VL to adapt to specific scenarios of police handwritten document recognition. Secondly, to test the recognition and extraction performance of various methods, a dataset was specifically constructed for the recognition and extraction of handwritten police documents. Finally, Multiple comparative experiments were conducted, and theoretical research and experimental results show that the new proposed PHDReader outperforms advanced OCR models and VLM in terms of recognition performance, stability and generalization ability.

title: PARL: Position-Aware Relation Learning Network for Document Layout Analysis
venue: arXiv (Cornell University)
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: Document layout analysis aims to detect and categorize structural elements (e.g., titles, tables, figures) in scanned or digital documents. Popular methods often rely on high-quality Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to merge visual features with extracted text. This dependency introduces two major drawbacks: propagation of text recognition errors and substantial computational overhead, limiting the robustness and practical applicability of multimodal approaches. In contrast to the prevailing multimodal trend, we argue that effective layout analysis depends not on text-visual fusion, but on a deep understanding of documents' intrinsic visual structure. To this end, we propose PARL (Position-Aware Relation Learning Network), a novel OCR-free, vision-only framework that models layout through positional sensitivity and relational structure. Specifically, we first introduce a Bidirectional Spatial Position-Guided Deformable Attention module to embed explicit positional dependencies among layout elements directly into visual features. Second, we design a Graph Refinement Classifier (GRC) to refine predictions by modeling contextual relationships through a dynamically constructed layout graph. Extensive experiments show PARL achieves state-of-the-art results. It establishes a new benchmark for vision-only methods on DocLayNet and, notably, surpasses even strong multimodal models on M6Doc. Crucially, PARL (65M) is highly efficient, using roughly four times fewer parameters than large multimodal models (256M), demonstrating that sophisticated visual structure modeling can be both more efficient and robust than multimodal fusion.

title: PACCF: Prescription-Aware Adaptive Confidence Fusion for Robust Medical Prescription OCR
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
screening_reason: Keyword-based recall aid only; not a final eligibility decision
abstract: The digitization of handwritten medical prescriptions remains a challenging task due to poor handwriting, variations in writing styles, image quality issues, and the presence of specialized pharmaceutical terminology. Although recent Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technologies have achieved significant progress in document understanding, their performance on medical prescriptions is often limited because most systems rely on a single recognition model and are therefore vulnerable to model-specific errors. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Prescription-Aware Adaptive Confidence Fusion (PACCF) framework for accurate and reliable medical prescription text recognition. The proposed approach combines the strengths of multiple OCR engines, namely TrOCR, PARSeq, EasyOCR, and PaddleOCR, to generate diverse recognition hypotheses from prescription text regions. Instead of selecting predictions based solely on confidence scores, PACCF introduces an adaptive fusion strategy that evaluates each candidate using four complementary reliability measures: confidence reliability, inter-model agreement, Gaussian consensus reliability, and medical lexical similarity. These factors are dynamically weighted through a Softmax-based mechanism, enabling data-driven decision making without manually tuned parameters. To further enhance recognition accuracy, a BK-Tree-based medical validation module is employed for efficient approximate matching and correction of pharmaceutical terms. Experimental results on a challenging handwritten prescription dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves both character-level and word-level recognition performance compared with individual OCR models and conventional fusion techniques. The findings suggest that integrating ensemble diversity, adaptive confidence modeling, and domain-specific medical knowledge provides an effective and scalable solution for automated prescription digitization and healthcare document processing
